summary: Young-earth creationist evangelist Kent Hovind built a dinosaur-themed ministry on diploma-mill degrees, went to prison for tax fraud, then ran an Alabama park where he sheltered a convicted child sex offender and a boy drowned.

evidence.note: birth in January 1953, probably Pensacola, childhood in East Peoria, Illinois
1989 move to Pensacola and founding of Creation Science Evangelism ministry
long segment on his diploma-mill PhD from Patriot Bible University and the flawed dissertation
tax protest from 1989, lawsuit against the IRS, selling guides to not paying taxes
sovereign citizen beliefs and 1998 court filing renouncing citizenship
2006 indictment on 58 tax counts, 2007 ten-year sentence, release by 2015-2016
donated land in Conecuh County, Alabama becomes the new Dinosaur Adventure Land
convicted child sex offender Chris Jones volunteers at the park; Hovind defends him
2019 visit where Hovind puts Jones and an 11-year-old boy in a cabin with one bed
March 2020 drowning of a seven-year-old in the park pond; Hovind hands out cards at hospital
serial marriages, body-slamming his third wife, 2021 domestic violence conviction

notes: Primary theme: young-earth creationism treated as pseudoscience; no dedicated creationism theme. The host repeatedly says Arkansas but corrects to Alabama (Conecuh County). Birthplace uncertain in transcript (Pensacola vs Illinois); origin US either way. Chris Jones floruit is an anchor year (2019 visit); his crimes date from 2001-2004.
